parts.title: Word List
parts.content:
Detailed Meanings

😎
coward[kauard]n.
A coward is a person who lacks courage to do risky or dangerous things.
→ A firefighter cannot be a coward. They have to be able to act quickly.
😎
delete[dili:t]v.
To delete something means to remove or erase written material.
→ Several lines had been deleted from her speech.
😎
firsthand[fa:rsthaend]adj.
If something is firsthand, then it is from an original source.
→ If you want firsthand knowledge, ask someone who saw it.
😎
earnest[a:rnist]adj.
If someone is earnest, then they are honest.
→ The child was very earnest when she told her mother how she broke the dish.
😎
ethnic[eθnik]adj.
If something is ethnic, then it is related to a group with a similar culture.
→ Many sections of the city are home to different ethnic communities.
😎
exclude[iksklu:d]v.
To exclude someone means to not accept them into a group.
→ Carol was excluded from the contest because her friend was a judge.
😎
fluent[flu:ənt]adj.
If someone is fluent in a language, then they are able to speak it very well.
→ She was so fluent in German that you’d have thought she was from Germany.
😎
imperial[impiarial]adj.
If something is imperial, then it is of, or related to an empire.
→ These old imperial coins were once used in the Roman Empire.
😎
inclusive[inklu:siv]adj.
If something is inclusive, then it is open to all groups and people in society.
→ A more inclusive event would have allowed children to attend.
😎
legislature[ledjisleitjar]n.
A legislature is the section of a government that makes laws.
→ The senator had served ten years in the national legislature.
😎
linguistic[lirjgwfstik]adj.
If something is linguistic, then it is concerned with language.
→ A linguistic way of studying culture focuses on words within that culture.
😎
monolingual[mdnah'rjgwal]adj.
If someone is monolingual, then they speak only one language.
→ In today’s global economy, being monolingual limits your opportunities.
😎
nationality[naejsnaelati]n.
Nationality is an identity based on the nation from which you come.
→ His nationality is German, but he speaks French, Spanish, and Korean.
😎
patriot[peitriat]n.
A patriot is someone who loves, supports, and defends their country.
→ Every year young patriots join their countries’ militaries.
😎
prosecute[prdsakju:t]v.
To prosecute someone means to take legal action against them.
→ They were prosecuted for fishing in the river without a permit.
😎
racial[reijal]adj.
If something is racial, then it is related to a race or races.
→ The differences between racial groups are physical characteristics and culture.
😎
solemn[salam]adj.
If something is solemn, then it is serious and honest.
→ The professor preferred a solemn relationship between him and his students.
😎
solidarity[sdladaerati]n.
Solidarity is a union formed from common responsibilities or interests.
→ All the citizens came together in a show of solidarity to create change.
😎
tact[taekt]n.
Tact is the ability to avoid offending people when dealing with problems.
→ Since both sides would not agree, it required someone with tact to make peace.
😎
undermine[Andamnain]v.
To undermine someone means to betray or weaken their efforts or authority.
→ The documents helped to undermine the workers’ trust in their bosses’ honesty.

sections.title: Exercise 1: Write a word that is similar in meaning to the underlined part.

questions.content: 1. No matter how much she begged, the older girls still did <u>not accept Suzy.</u>
questions.explanation: excluded (v): not accepted into a group.

questions.content: 2. <u>Language</u> based approaches are the best way to learn about a culture.
questions.explanation: Linguistic (adj): concerned with language.

questions.content: 3. Constant changes were <u>weakening the</u> project’s chances of being finished on time.
questions.explanation: undermining (v): weakening efforts or authority.

questions.content: 4. The boy made a <u>serious and honest</u> promise to his parents that he would never again cheat.
questions.explanation: solemn (adj): serious and honest.

questions.content: 5. The movie director gave the actors and actresses a <u>personal and original view</u> of the newly completed movie.
questions.explanation: firsthand (adj): from an original source.

questions.content: 6. Everyone knew that Luke studied Chinese. But no one knew he was <u>able to speak it very well.</u>
questions.explanation: fluent (adj): able to speak a language very well.

questions.content: 7. The teacher was waiting for one of the students to be <u>honest</u> about what had happened on the playground.
questions.explanation: earnest (adj): honest.

questions.content: 8. The Internet has made talking to people everywhere very natural. As a result, having <u>a sense of common support for your ideas is</u> easy.
questions.explanation: solidarity (n): a union formed from common responsibilities or interests.

questions.content: 9. Though he looked Greek, his <u>identity based on the country he came from was Mexican.</u>
questions.explanation: nationality (n): an identity based on the nation from which you come.

questions.content: 10. Today, no one lives in the old royal palace. Instead, it’s part <u>of the university.</u>
questions.explanation: imperial (adj): of, or related to an empire.

sections.title: Exercise 2: Write C if the italicized word is used correctly. Write I if the word is used incorrectly.

questions.content: 1. Peter is so earnest. He made more money than anyone I know.
questions.explanation: I: Earnest means honest, not wealthy.

questions.content: 2. If you like ethnic foods, then you like foods from other cultures.
questions.explanation: C: Ethnic means related to a group with a similar culture.

questions.content: 3. Though it’s the same language, there are linguistic differences between the two areas.
questions.explanation: C: Linguistic means concerned with language.

questions.content: 4. The patriot is an amazing bird. It can repeat anything you tell it.
questions.explanation: I: A patriot is someone who loves their country, not a bird (parrot).

questions.content: 5. If you want someone to care for your cattle, you should call a coward.
questions.explanation: I: A coward lacks courage; a cowherd cares for cattle.

questions.content: 6. The boy said that the test was unfair, and his classmates showed solidarity and agreed.
questions.explanation: C: Solidarity means common support.

questions.content: 7. The king said the princes had undermined his authority when they issued new orders.
questions.explanation: C: Undermined means weakened efforts or authority.

questions.content: 8. We deleted all the words that were spelled wrong.
questions.explanation: C: Deleted means removed or erased.

questions.content: 9. “I’m sorry you can’t eat here. This restaurant is inclusive.”
questions.explanation: I: Inclusive means open to all groups; exclusive would mean restricted.

questions.content: 10. The road going to the farmhouse is monolingual, so watch cars coming your way.
questions.explanation: I: Monolingual means speaking one language. A road might be one-way.

questions.content: 11. He had seen the battle firsthand in old movies.
questions.explanation: I: Firsthand means from an original source. Seeing it in movies is not firsthand.

questions.content: 12. If someone goes to court, then they are judged by the legislature.
questions.explanation: I: A legislature makes laws; a court or jury judges.

questions.content: 13. This city’s history is important. It was once the imperial capital.
questions.explanation: C: Imperial means related to an empire.

questions.content: 14. His friends had left him alone in the library, but he didn’t mind being solemn.
questions.explanation: I: Solemn means serious and honest, it doesn't mean being alone.

questions.content: 15. The criminals were prosecuted for the crimes they had committed.
questions.explanation: C: Prosecuted means legal action was taken against them.

questions.content: 16. That college excludes anyone who has low test scores.
questions.explanation: C: Exclude means not accept into a group.

questions.content: 17. Many people wonder about her nationality. However, he knows where she’s from.
questions.explanation: C: Nationality is the nation you come from.

questions.content: 18. The mothers covered their children’s heads because the rain was so fluent.
questions.explanation: I: Fluent refers to speaking a language well, not heavy rain.

questions.content: 19. I liked all the cars, but I bought the racial car because it was the fastest.
questions.explanation: I: Racial means related to a race; it doesn't describe a car.

questions.content: 20. His method had a lot of tact. Soon, everyone agreed with his point of view.
questions.explanation: C: Tact is the ability to avoid offending people.

parts.title: Comprehensive Reading
parts.content:
The Editor’s Choice

A newspaper editor sat at his desk and stared at the flashing cursor on his computer’s screen. He didn’t know if he should delete the article he had just written or go ahead and publish it. He was scared and filled with doubt.

The empire had passed a new law stating that citizens could only use the imperial language. The editor disagreed with the law and decided to write an article about why it was wrong. He felt that the new law excluded people of different nationalities and racial and ethnic backgrounds. He had firsthand knowledge of what it feels like not to be fluent in the imperial language because he was from a remote part of the empire.

He felt that the empire shouldn’t be monolingual and should be more inclusive. Yet he was afraid that he would get in trouble for having this belief. Many would say that he was not a patriot—that he didn’t love the empire. But he didn’t wish to undermine the authority of the empire. He wanted to argue that the empire could be stronger if it accepted people of various cultures and beliefs.

At last, he decided to stop being a coward and to be earnest about how he felt. He wrote the article. It wasn’t rude or angry, but rather, very solemn and intelligent. The next day it was published in all the papers.

Everyone was impressed by his tact and showed solidarity with his ideas. He expected to be arrested any day, but the police never came. Surprisingly, instead of being prosecuted, he became a hero. The legislature changed the law, and people from many linguistic backgrounds praised him.

sections.title: Part A: Mark each statement T for true or F for false.

questions.content: 1. The editor felt the imperial law excluded people of different nationalities and racial and ethnic backgrounds.
questions.explanation: T

questions.content: 2. The legislature prosecuted the editor for undermining the authority of the empire.
questions.explanation: F: The legislature changed the law.

questions.content: 3. The editor was not fluent in the empire’s language.
questions.explanation: T

questions.content: 4. Everyone was impressed by the editor’s tact and showed solidarity with his ideas.
questions.explanation: T

questions.content: 5. The article wasn’t solemn and intelligent, but rather rude and angry.
questions.explanation: F: The article wasn't rude or angry, but rather, solemn and intelligent.

questions.content: 1. Where was the editor sitting when the cursor was ready to delete his article?
questions.explanation: The editor was sitting at his desk when the cursor was ready to delete his article.

questions.content: 2. After the editor decided not to be a coward but be earnest, what did he do?
questions.explanation: After the editor decided not to be a coward but be earnest, he wrote the article.

questions.content: 3. If the empire accepted other languages, what did the editor think would happen?
options: The empire would lose its culture.
questions.explanation: The empire would be stronger.

questions.content: 4. Why was the editor afraid to say that the empire should be more inclusive?
options: He was afraid that he would get in trouble for having this belief.
He was afraid of losing his nationality.
He was afraid no one would read his article.
He was afraid of being physically hurt by a patriot.
questions.correctAnswer: He was afraid that he would get in trouble for having this belief.
questions.explanation: He was afraid that he would get in trouble for having this belief.

questions.content: 5. What did the editor write about being vocal?
options: "Never undermine the authority of the empire."
questions.explanation: The editor wrote, “Don't be afraid to be vocal.”
